```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{bash}

  
cd ../data/raw
pwd

curl -O http://owl.fish.washington.edu/nightingales/C_gigas/filtered_174gm_A_BiGosperm_L006_R1.fastq.gz

gunzip filtered_174gm_A_BiGosperm_L006_R1.fastq.gz

```

Curl is a pre-downloaded program that allows you to download data that exists on the web.

relative path is best because it can be used in any computer vs. absolute path which would only work in Raven

..except if downloading a software. Absolute path is good and really the only option for a software because that's where the software lives

##FastQC and running software

/home/shared/FastQC-0.12.1/fastqc runs the software

Raven programs are all stored on /home/shared/..

```{bash}
/home/shared/FastQC-0.12.1/fastqc -h
/home/shared/FastQC-0.12.1/fastqc ../data/raw/filtered_174gm_A_BiGosperm_L006_R1.fastq
```

best practice is putting output files into output folder
